d_en: Regarding the alleged scams in the Delhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA), the AAP claims that if properly investigated, the Union finance minister will not be able to defend himself.
AAP leader Ashutosh says, "This is an open and shut case, that is, the evidence against him (Arun Jaitley) is solid."
"For the last ten years, he has been raising his voice against corruption in the DDCA," Ashutosh told the BBC.
No one has paid as much attention to it as they should have.
Kirti Azad had exposed the alleged scams in DDCA.
To conclude, though he did not directly name BJP leader and Union Finance Minister Arun Jaitley, these are alleged scams when Jaitley was the president of DDCAA.
The Aam Aadmi Party and Congress hold the finance minister responsible for these scams.
That is why both parties have demanded his resignation.
In an exclusive interview with BBC Hindi, Ashutosh claimed that there was "very solid evidence" against the finance minister.
"As far as the evidence is concerned, I say it is an open and shut case," he says.
If investigated honestly, it would be impossible for the finance minister to save himself.
Arun Jaitley has called the allegations "baseless."
He has filed a defamation case against Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, Ashutosh and four other AAP leaders in a Delhi court.
He has also filed a criminal case against them.
According to Ashutosh, Kirti Azad's suspension is wrong as it is not an internal matter of the BJP.
"Kirti Azad has not raised any question on the functioning of the finance minister, which is related to his government," he says.
This is an issue outside the BJP.
If they are raising the issue of corruption, the BJP should back Kirti Azad.
The BJP had suspended Kirti Azad from the party, saying he was involved in anti-party activities.
The Aam Aadmi Party has condemned the BJP's decision.
But the Aam Aadmi Party itself is also anti-party.
ref_claims: भारतीय जनता पार्टी (भाजपा) के निलंबित सांसद कीर्ति आज़ाद के समर्थन में आम आदमी पार्टी खुलकर सामने आ गई है.

d_en: An arrest warrant has been issued against a Tunisian national, Sarhan bin Abdulmajid Fakht, in this connection.
A warrant has been issued for five more suspects who are Moroccan residents.
Meanwhile, some security officials with knowledge of the investigation say people connected to the drug trade played a key role in planning and raising funds for the attacks.
The warrant for the arrest of the Jihad Tunisian states that Fakht started the Jihad in Madrid in the middle of last year.
A Spanish court issued warrants for six people, saying two men planned the attack.
The other four were among the group that placed 13 bombs on four trains on 11 March.
Already 19 people are in custody in connection with the investigation.
More than 200 people were killed in the bombings in Madrid.

ref_en: Authorities in Spain say the man responsible for the March 11 bombings in Madrid has been identified.

d_en: In his recent visit to Ghana, we had the opportunity to see Ahmadinejad up close and evaluate his eight-year tenure.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad looked unhappy as he walked down the road to the airport in Ghana's capital, Accra.
On his arrival in Ghana, he inspected the Guard of Honour in the line of duty.
Listen to the national anthems of Iran and Ghana.
Ghanaian President John Mahama began escorting Ahmadinejad to the airport's terminal building.
It was then that Ahmadinejad moved his hands round and round in the air.
He wanted to shake hands with the people present there.
Ahmadinejad then began to leave the airport.
Just then, dozens of students dressed in white T-shirts walked up to him to say hello.
Ahmadinejad looked at them and smiled.
Nothing gives them more happiness than a crowd of people.
Sitting on the stage in the popular Acra, the Iranian president was enjoying the image he had built over the past eight years.
A Ghanaian resident shouted, "We want you, we want you, we want you."
"Ahmadinejad has been very different from the previous Iranian presidents." "" "He said,"
He continued to wear the cheap Sea Jacket, "he said. "....?
Continue to keep a shaven beard......?
These things caused the Iranian middle class to bow down to them.
Ahmadinejad wanted the same thing.
He sought the support of marginal working-class people such as farmers and taxi drivers.
The desire for more power was met with sharp opposition to Iran's nuclear program.
Western countries and the United Nations imposed a range of sanctions on Iran.
Ahmadinejad is not afraid of these restrictions.
The more they protested, the more they provoked them.
And that's when his stature grew bigger.
"I'm pretty sure we took Ahmadinejad more seriously than necessary," says Ryan Crocker, a former US ambassador who has been most involved with Iran over the past three decades.
"Ahmadinejad likes to get angry.
They like to be attacked from every corner of a civilised society, "he said in a statement.
But I think it doesn't make much of a difference in terms of Iran-related policies.

d_en: By taking regular courses, such people are coming forward to become professional astrologers who find it a little difficult to call Panditji or Shastriji.

From generation to generation, this traditional form of study, driven by the guru-shishya tradition, is changing rapidly, computers have replaced the booklet and the Chutia Pandit has been replaced by English-speaking youths wearing jeans.
About twenty-five universities in India offer degrees in astrology after formal studies, which have seen a huge influx of enrollees these days.
S Ganesh, a professor of astrology at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan in Delhi, believes that "when people can take up subjects like cooking and home decor as a profession, why not astrology?"
Regarding the ever-growing belief in astrology, Ila Shukla, daughter of a famous astrologer, says that "life is no longer as simple as it used to be.
In this age of stress and competition, astrology is helpful in making life easier to some extent, so its popularity is increasing.
Sheela Parkhi, an astrology student, says, "It is a respectable profession, with a lot of money, and can be done sitting at home, making it an ideal subject for women."
Until a few years ago, the number of astrologers in Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan ranged from 50 to 100, but this year it has increased to 800.

Explaining the reason for the increase in the number of people reading this subject, S. Ganesh says, "Earlier, people of a particular caste used to study it, but now the doors of astrology have opened for everyone.
"But there are people who believe that opening the door to everyone doesn't mean that everyone is good.

d_en: Judge PD Kode had on Tuesday convicted four members of the Memon family out of 123 accused in the case.
The court was scheduled to pronounce the sentence on Wednesday itself but the defence lawyers sought more time to argue on what the punishment should be, which was accepted by the court.
Mumbai was rocked by a series of 12 bomb blasts on March 12, 1993, which killed 257 people and injured over 700.
Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam has asked the court to award the death penalty to the convicts.
The defence counsel, on the other hand, argues that his client has already spent 13 years in jail and should now be acquitted.
As the arguments from both sides remained inconclusive, the judge said the verdict on the sentence would be pronounced on Thursday.
The verdict on the eight other accused will be delivered on Thursday itself.
The court has said that it will pronounce the verdict by dividing the accused into groups of eight.
The case is considered one of the most complex and lengthy in Indian legal history.
The trial in the case went on for over a decade and 686 witnesses appeared and a chargesheet of about ten thousand pages was filed.
The court's verdict in the case is awaited not only by the accused but also by the Special Task Force probing the case, the CBI and the Crime Branch of the Mumbai Police.
ref_claims: मुंबई की विशेष टाडा अदालत 1993 में हुए सिलसिलेवार बम धमाकों में दोषी ठहराए गए चार लोगों के ख़िलाफ़ गुरुवार को सज़ा सुनाएगी.
ref_en: A special TADA court in Mumbai will on Thursday pronounce the quantum of sentence against the four men convicted in the 1993 serial bomb blasts.

d_en: Recently, a US Senate intelligence committee came down heavily on the CIA for exaggerating evidence about alleged weapons of mass destruction in Iraq.
President Bush firmly defended his decision to take military action in Iraq, saying he had no choice.
He acknowledged that weapons of mass destruction had not yet been found in Iraq, but reiterated that the United States had to take this step to defend itself.
"I had two options, either I would listen to a madman (Saddam Hussein) or I would defend the United States," Bush said.
If I had such options, I would continue to defend America every time in the future.
Recently, a Senate committee in its report took the CIA to task, raising several serious questions about its functioning.
Iraq is becoming a major issue in the US presidential election.
Democratic candidate John Kerry, who is challenging President Bush, has said the decision to take military action in Iraq has made the American people more vulnerable.
A BBC correspondent from Washington says the issue of the country's security has become a major issue in the campaigns of both candidates.

ref_en: U.S. President George W. Bush, who has been heavily criticized for his military action in Iraq, has once again justified his decision.

d_en: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has formally requested the President to remove Justice Ganguly from his post.
The matter was also echoed in Parliament on Friday, with calls in both houses for Justice Ganguly's ouster.
But constitutional experts have questioned how legal action can be taken against Justice Ganguly if no FIR has been lodged by the victim.
However, a committee of Supreme Court judges has prima facie confirmed that one of its own interns was subjected to abusive behaviour against Justice Ganguly.
By the time the incident took place, Justice Ganguly had finished his last day's work.
In such a situation, the Supreme Court cannot take any action against them.

According to the website of the West Bengal Human Rights Commission, under the Human Rights Act 1993, the chairperson or a member of the commission can only be removed by the president on the recommendation of the Supreme Court.

If the commission's chairman or a member is accused of misconduct or does not deserve it, the Supreme Court conducts its own inquiry on the recommendation of the President, and if the investigation finds the allegation to be true, the Supreme Court recommends his removal to the President.
In addition, the President may remove the Chairman or a member of the Commission for any of the following reasons:

ref_en: The demand for the sacking of former Supreme Court judge Ashok Kumar Ganguly as the chairperson of the West Bengal Human Rights Commission, who is accused of sexually harassing a female trainee lawyer, is gaining momentum.

d_en: The buzz at the Mohali stadium was such that the crowd suddenly began to swell up to see Sachin set a world record.
But finally, there was disappointment, Sachin missed out and was dismissed for 94.
Now, perhaps for some more time, cricket lovers will have to wait for Sachin's 35th century.
Sehwag's innings was memorable, aside from the disappointment of missing out on a century from Sachin.
While Sehwag completed his century playing on top of an individual score of 95, other India batsmen also showed signs of being in fine form.
The start of the third day was also very exciting.
Sehwag and Rahul Dravid batted brilliantly in the first hour, sharing a century stand for the second wicket to give India a solid foundation.
At 216, India suffered their first blow when Rahul Dravid was dismissed by Mohammed Shami.
Dravid returned to the pavilion with his 36th half-century.
He was replaced by Master Blaster Sachin Tendulkar, who had high expectations and also made you feel in form by having a great straight drive.
On the other hand, Sehwag played an aggressive innings to complete his 150.
He completed these runs in 191 balls of play, with the help of 18 fours and 2 sixes.
Sometime later, Sehwag scored his highest score in India.
His previous highest score in India was 164 at Kanpur.
Nakhush Inzamam changed the ball several times in the match today.
A lot of time was also wasted, but captain Inzamam was not at all happy with the ball being replaced.
The two umpires spoke to Inzamam and the match started.
Sehwag's fine innings eventually ended on 173.
In an attempt to hit a pull shot, Sehwag took an easy catch off Johanna.
The only reason for Sehwag's dismissal was that Inzamam kept the field open and the bowlers were not giving away runs at all.
Captain Sourav Ganguly took his place, but it has to be said that he is absolutely in his rhythm.
ref_claims: मोहाली टेस्ट का तीसरा दिन पूरी तरह वीरेंदर सहवाग के नाम रहा लेकिन चर्चा में रहे सचिन तेंदुलकर.
आख़िर मास्टर ब्लास्टर 35वाँ शतक बनाते-बनाते चूक गए.
ref_en: The third day of the Mohali Test was entirely in Virender Sehwag's name but Sachin Tendulkar was the talk of the town.
Eventually, the Master Blaster missed out on scoring his 35th century.

d_en: He faxed his resignation at the behest of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.
His resignation has been accepted.
Jharkhand Mukti Morcha general secretary and MP Sunil Mehta on Saturday confirmed Soren's resignation, saying it was making him a victim of a political conspiracy.
"We met the prime minister and handed over the resignation of Shibu Soren to him," said Sunil Mehta.
We have assured them that with the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha government.

"The BJP government in Jharkhand has re-opened the case for political reasons in view of the upcoming Assembly elections and it is a sheer political conspiracy," Sunil Mehto said after his meeting with the Prime Minister, according to news agency PTI.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Ghulam Nabi Azad confirmed to reporters in Delhi that a Jharkhand Mukti Morcha delegation had sent Soren's faxed resignation to the prime minister.
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had on Friday written to Shibu Soren asking him to resign after a prolonged controversy.
The Bharatiya Janata Party has welcomed Shibu Soren's resignation, saying the prime minister has done a "good job" of taking the decision.
Senior BJP leader Sushma Swaraj said in Delhi: "If the Prime Minister had taken this decision four days ago, the uproar in Parliament could have been stopped."
Shibu Soren has been missing since a trial court in Jharkhand issued arrest warrants against him in a murder case in Chirudih, then Bihar, in 1975 and has not even been to Parliament.
This caused an uproar in Parliament for almost the entire week with the opposition demanding the Prime Minister to sack Shibu Soren.
Morcha MP Sunil Mehto said on Saturday that Shibu Soren's bail plea will be heard in the Ranchi High Court on Monday and further strategy will be decided if his bail is granted.
There was speculation over the hearing of Shibu Soren's bail plea for several days, but the matter finally came up before the High Court on Friday.

ref_en: India's Coal Minister and Jharkhand Mukti Morcha leader Shibu Soren resigned as a minister on Saturday after a week-long controversy.

d_en: A government spokesperson said that the Bodo tribe has objected to a scene in the film.
The film shows a Bodo rebel cutting off a prisoner's ear and presenting it to his girlfriend, which the Bodos say affects their image.
"In the film Tango Charlie, the scene of ear-cutting and offering presents the Bodo people as ferocious rapists," says Alang Narzari, advisor to the All Bodo Students'Union.
Bodo MP Urkha Gaira Brahma said it would not be acceptable to anyone.
Following street protests in Bodo-dominated areas, the screening of the film has been banned across the state.
But the Bodo people are not satisfied with this.
The All Bodo Students'Union has demanded that film director Mani Shankar publicly apologise for hurting the sentiments of the Bodo people.
They have also demanded from the censor board that the controversial scene be removed from the film.
Though the Bodo rebels have been threatening to cut off the hands and feet of the hostages for ransom, there is no evidence so far that they have ever done so.
The Bodos have been demanding that a Bodo-majority part of Assam be declared a separate state, but last year most organisations agreed to the region being declared an autonomous region.

ref_en: In India, the government of the state of Assam has banned the screening of the film Tango Charlie.
The ban has been imposed following protests by the Bodo tribe.

In 2015, Justin Trudeau said that India does not have as many Sikhs in its cabinet as he has.

d_en: Iran has been warned that economic sanctions could be imposed against it if it does not stop uranium enrichment work.
The proposal is expected to be discussed at a Security Council meeting on Monday.
Iran says it has a nuclear program to produce electricity.
But the five permanent members of the Security Council are skeptical that Iran wants to build a nuclear bomb.
Iran has previously refused to stop uranium enrichment, refusing to comply with the Security Council.
France, Britain and Germany have drafted a resolution outlining what materials should not be sold to Iran to prevent it from developing nuclear weapons.
The proposal has been prepared following concerns from Russia and China.
Both countries have the right to veto the resolution.
By the way, Russia is building a nuclear power plant in Iran, so China has to take oil from Iran.
European officials are hoping the proposal will be put to a vote before Christmas.

ref_en: At the United Nations, France, Britain and Germany have presented a new draft resolution calling for a cut in Iran's nuclear program.

d_en: If you don't want to chat with certain friends on Facebook or pass your posts on to them, be active in your Facebook Messenger chat.
Go to Facebook Messenger's chat settings and then go to Advanced Settings.
There, you'll see "Turn of Chat for Only Some Friends."
Now search for friends'posts on Facebook, too, and you won't see anyone you name online.
Be sure to save once you've made the settings.
This will get you rid of unwanted chat friends.
It's also not too hard to do if you don't want the chosen ones to show up online.
For such people, you turn off the chat feature so you don't see them online.
Make a full-length video while you're sharing your posts so you also have the option to keep some people away from that post.
First, type in your post, then click "Friends" at the bottom left of the box.
Then go to "More Options" and then select "Custom."
After that, you'll see the "Don't Share With" option.
Write down the names of the people you don't want to share this post with.
Don't forget to click "Save Changes."
After that, your posts will no longer be visible to those whose names you wrote.

d_en: A woman getting a knife massage may sound a little awkward, but it's true.
Massage parlours in the East Asian country of Taiwan massage people on a large scale with knives.
It is called "dauliao," which means "massage with a knife" or "knife therapy" in Chinese.
It is very common in Chinese medicine.
This practice of knife massage there dates back to about 2000 years.
It was started by Buddhist monks.
This therapy also flourished in Japan during the Tang dynasty about a thousand years ago.
This tradition of knife massage reached Taiwan during the Chinese Civil War in the late 1940s.
Today, however, the practice of this therapy has almost died out in China and Japan.
However, it is still very popular in Taiwan.
An education center to teach this therapy has also been opened in Taipei, the capital of Taiwan.
It is called The Ancient Art of Knife Massage Daoliao I-Jing Educational Center.
The education center has about 36 branches throughout Taiwan.
Of these, 15 have been opened in the last five years alone.
People from all over the world are taught the art of knife massage here.
People from France, Canada, Hong Kong, and Japan come to Taiwan to learn this therapy.
Also read: People ask, Where do you touch? In recent times, there has been a huge increase in people taking this therapy in Taiwan.
Benefits of Knife Massage Today, people are using these massage knives to heal wounds, improve sleep, and also to heal chronic body aches.
Knife therapy targets pressure points in the same way that acupressure therapy does in Chinese medicine.
These are called Qi-doors.
Hsiao Mei-fang, the director of one such massage center in Taiwan, says he entered the world of Knife Massage 15 years ago.
Before this, she used to do beauty treatments and meridian massage.

d_en: The economic shock caused by Corona is far more severe than any financial crisis, OECD Secretary-General Enkel Guria has said.
He told the BBC that it was a dream to believe that the world would recover quickly from this situation.
The OECD urged governments in all countries to increase their spending so that more people can be tested and treated faster.
Enkel Guria recently said that the world's economy will slow down by 1.5% if the corona takes the form of a pandemic, but now it seems to be more.

The secretary-general of the defunct Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, Ankel Guria, said it was not yet clear how many jobs would be lost and how many companies would be shut down, but that the economy would suffer in the coming days.
He says many of the world's biggest countries could face recessions in the coming months, meaning the economy could continue to decline for two consecutive quarters.
"Even if not all over the world, many of the world's economies, especially the large ones, will either see no growth or decline," he said.
This means that not only will world growth slow down, but it will take longer to get back on track in the future.
The big shock, said Enkel Guria, could be far greater than the economic devastation of Corona, the 2008 recession, and the extremist attacks of 9/11.
"We don't know how long it will take to solve the problem of unemployment caused by this because we don't know how many people are going to be unemployed because of this," he said.
We don't even know how many businesses are struggling and on the verge of closure because of this and how long it will take for things to get back to normal.
"The whole world is trying to deal with the Corona epidemic.

d_en: In its annual report released in Rome, the UN Food and Agriculture Organization says the world is losing its battle against hunger.
The report notes that between 2001 and 2002, more than 850 million people worldwide were malnourished, and this number is steadily increasing.
According to the UN food agency, more than 810 million people are undernourished in developing countries alone, and the number continues to grow.
The agency has said it was promised eight years ago that the number would be halved by 2015.
But little progress has been made in this direction.
Target However, the agency has expressed hope that this goal is still achievable.
The report urges rich countries to do more on their part to end hunger.
The assistant director-general of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization has said that the international community has not understood the economic benefits of fighting hunger.
The report refers to areas of the world where the largest number of people suffer from hunger and malnutrition.
There are 35 countries in the world with the highest food shortages, most of them in Africa.
But worsening conditions in China and India have also contributed to the problem.
The report highlights that the problem of malnutrition is not limited to developing countries.
Even in the so-called industrially rich countries, this number has reached 9 million.

The two leaders had insulted and threatened each other over the past year with the words'Thingoji Rocket Man'and'Weak old man '.

Why is news important?
That's because the world has been concerned for decades about North Korea's nuclear weapons development program.
North Korea has conducted six illegal underground tests of nuclear weapons and has fired several long-range missiles.
North Korea has said it could launch a nuclear attack on the United States.
The extent of truth in that claim has yet to be determined, but North Korea may be willing to attack its neighbors.
His offer to give up nuclear weapons is quite surprising.
Why did North Korea do this now?
It is possible that North Korea was forced to negotiate because of years of sanctions.
It is possible that North Korea believes that Donald Trump can be manipulated.
It is also possible that North Korea has decided to seek recognition as a serious nuclear state.
What will happen now?
Complex diplomacy will begin quickly.
It is not yet known whether the talks will take place and who will join the two leaders.
It is also not yet known what North Korea wants in return for a meeting with Donald Trump.
North Korea has not yet made any commitments.
Even if it is willing to give up its nuclear weapons, the key issue will be how to prove it.
North Korea has reneged on promises in the past as well.

d_en: Bipin Rawat Helicopter Crash Enquiry: The tri-services inquiry set up by the Ministry of Defence to investigate the causes of death of 14 people, including Chief of Defence Staff General Bipin Rawat, who died in a helicopter crash in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu on December 8, is likely to be completed within the next 2 weeks.

Statements are being recorded and in one or two cases, some people have changed the account of events, he said.

The tragic accident took place on December 8 (Wednesday), when a Mi-17V5 took off from Sulur airbase in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu, and made a short journey of about 30 minutes.

d_en: Sanjay Tank, Ahmedabad: Usually, students feel confused as the exam approaches.
Then be it school students or college students.
Students study the previous year's papers for preparation before the exam and to understand the paper style.

Often senior students do not get the paper despite asking for it or students have to take the help of the library in which time is wasted at the time of the exam itself but now the students of MSc IT of GLS have found a solution to that problem.
These students have covered 10,000 papers of all streams in one mobile application.
Pranjal, Rishabh, Jeenali, students of MSc IT, a joint initiative of Gujarat University Library and GLS University, have developed a mobile application called Saarthi.
The application covers 10,000 papers from all streams since 2014.
In which now students will be able to prepare by studying the previous year's question papers at home.
Pranjal states that at the time of the exam, one has to either depend on the senior for the old questions or run to the library to get the paper.
This problem was also experienced by us, so a solution was needed.
That is why Sarathi has created the app.
Another feature of this app is that Gujarati English and Hindi all medium papers are also available in the app.
The app has different parts like BA, Bcom, BSc which have a collection of papers.
Students'mentors Dineshbhai and Vishalbhai say that students will now be able to get the paper for study with a single click on the mobile while sitting at home.
Significantly, this app will not only benefit lakhs of students studying in Gujarat University but will also inspire other universities to start such an app for their students.

As a result, there was heavy rainfall in some parts of the district.
But given the current situation in the district, farmers who have already planted grain crops in their fields are seen to be worried.
Due to the cloudy weather for the last few days, farmers in the district were expecting rain.
But the clouds continue to move hand in hand, causing disappointment among the farmers.
Paddy crops require adequate water which farmers have no other option than natural water.
He was seen sitting with his hands on the farmers'heads.
Also, those who have planted maize crops are seeing an infestation of mites and other pests.
Due to which the farmers who had sown the crop during the interim rains are looking worried.
Along with this, the district is also seeing sunshine as the monsoon continues to pass by, and somewhere the kingdom of clouds is surrounded and a humid atmosphere is being created.

d_en: They were lured to eat to teach the fish to count.

This finding by a team of psychologists from the University of Padova in Italy may seem absurd at first glance, but it raises the interesting question of how we estimate people, animals, or things by looking at their numbers.
Humans are believed to have an innate ability to count.
But research has proved that there are other beings besides humans who understand the difference between less and more, that is, for them ten things are not equal to a hundred.
It is of great importance in the forest.
Animals, for example, need to understand which of the two sources of food is larger or which group of mates is larger in order to reduce the likelihood of becoming involved and becoming prey.
Counting, however, is the difference between making a distinction between two groups being small and large, and counting the members of each group.
One assumption is that animals use counts for small groups and adopt a proportional system for large groups.
On this basis, some fish count up to a number of four, but come up with a proportional system.
Fish, like children, learn to count as they age.
Newborn fish can distinguish between one or two and even three or four.
But they develop the ability to distinguish between four and eight within 20 to 40 days.
Newborn fish thus have an innate ability to count to four, but the proportional system they learn as they age.
Experiments, however, raise the question of how to teach math to fish?
The simple answer is to offer them food as a reward.
The researchers placed the fish in a rectangular tank and made points at each end.
Place the food at the end where the highest points were made.

Mandal's contribution I come from a lower middle-class family.

"Traditionalists in the church believe that the activities of these people are against the will of God.

According to Sunil, the meeting in Chennai was aimed at getting to know the problems of homosexuals and is a start.

d_en: Aadhaar is a 12-digit identity card linked to biometrics i.e. fingerprints, eyeglasses, and photographs.
When the government project was launched in 2009 during UPA-II, the government machinery repeatedly assured that it was optional and would not be made mandatory.
Then gradually the government made it mandatory from the back door to get the right to work and pension under NREGA.
When the Supreme Court said in September 2013 that people could not be denied their rights because of this, a shrewd officer from the Ministry of Rural Development found a way for the government.
Government orders would have written the court order in the first line, as well as the second line - if there is no Aadhaar number, the person should be assisted in Aadhaar registration.
The story doesn't end here...
Just as the Supreme Court order was twisted as it came to Mantralaya, the Mantralaya order (people to be registered in Aadhaar) was further twisted as it reached the district.
As a result, those who did not have Aadhaar were gradually cut off.

The story doesn't end here - as people's names were cut off for not having Aadhaar, without their knowledge, the government started claiming that these people were'fake'who have been caught because of Aadhaar.

d_en: Speaking to the people of DM village in Gopalganj, he did this to dispel the superstition of the villagers associated with a widowed cook.
Widow Sunita Devi is a cook at a government middle school in Kalyanpur village of Gopalganj district.
According to the information, Sunita was removed on the basis of some allegations in February last year and she was not even given a chance to present her explanation.
After nearly two years of struggle, Sunita was able to regain her job this Monday.

According to Sunita, a widow cook at the school, local journalist Abhay Rajan, on the third day of returning to work, villagers stopped Sunita from cooking and locked her up at the school, questioning her character and considering her inauspicious.
In such a situation, Sunita once again sought help from District Magistrate Rahul Kumar on Thursday.
This time, he ensured Sunita's return to work in the presence of senior officials.
Rahul explains, "I felt there were multiple aspects to the whole affair.
In such a situation, it is necessary to go and explain to people.
I decided to hurt people's superstitions by eating food from Sunita's own hands in school.
After this unique intervention of the district collector, on Saturday, Sunita along with the rest of the cooks made khichdi and chokha for about seven hundred children.
"Today, all the teachers and children ate my hand-crafted food," Sunita told the BBC as she ate the mid-day meal with the DM school children.
There was no protest from the villagers.
Sunita explains that DM sahab's enthusiasm has increased after eating the food.
Kalyanpur panchayat chief Ramdev Paswan told the BBC: "The DM sahab's words have had a good impact.
People have understood what he said.
His thinking has changed, his conscience has awakened.
However, he also believes that some people are no longer protesting even for fear of the administration's action.
Sunita's two children also study in the same school where she works.

d_en: It may be noted that as per the census conducted five years ago, the Asiatic lion population in Gujarat was 523.
Prime Minister Modi also immediately shared the good news with the countrymen through his social media.
But at a time when the coronavirus outbreak is raging across the country, could this exercise to find out the number of lions not have been dangerous?
So, was there no danger of the virus reaching the animals in the forests at all? "he asked.
All these questions must be running through your mind.
But let us tell you that this time the exercise of counting lions was completely different from the one that was done every five years.
This time too, the lion count was to be done as per the traditional method during 5th-6th June.
The lion count of this time was not traditionally done with a large number of officers, volunteers.

But with the announcement of the lockdown, there was a fear of the virus spreading from humans to wild animals by going to the forest with so much manpower and counting the lions, so this time as a precaution, the unconventional and safe way to find out the number of Asiatic lions living in Gujarat was adopted as'Poonam observation '.
The traditional way of counting lions was the traditional way of counting lions every five years.
It was attended by a large number of officials, volunteers from NGOs, etc.
So that there is transparency in the calculation process.
Thus, this calculation, traditionally done, can be completed in just two days.
This includes the primary stage and the final stage count.
The traditional method uses a block-counting method.
In this system, the staff and volunteers engaged in this work are posted at different water points in the area allotted to them.
This is done by keeping a close watch on the lions living in these areas and estimating their numbers.
This method counts the number of lions that have come to drink water at least once in the past 24 hours.
Thus, in this method, officials and volunteers get an estimate of the number of lions by keeping a close eye on them.
The method of Poonam observation was adopted by the Forest Department of Gujarat as it was not safe to take a large number of people inside the forest this time.
Let us tell you that Poonam Avalokan is a monthly in-house exercise, in which only forest department personnel can participate.
According to this method, the field staff and officers for the counting of lions are assigned to them to get a complete 24-hour estimate of the number of lions in the assigned area.

d_en: Republic Day Parade Who started the tradition of celebrating Republic Day?
The first President of the country, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, declared India a full republic by hoisting the flag with a 21-gun salute on 26 January 1950.
Since then every year this day is celebrated as Republic Day and this day is a national holiday throughout the country.
When did India adopt its constitution?
India is a union of states.
It is a republic with a parliamentary system of government.
The republic is governed by the Constitution of India which was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950.
The concept of Five Year Plan in the Indian Constitution is derived from which constitution?
The concept of a five-year plan in the Indian constitution was taken from the Soviet Union (USSR).
Who hoists the flag on Republic Day?
The first citizen of the country, the President, participates in the Republic Day celebrations and also hoists the national flag.
Who hoists the national flag at the Republic Day celebrations in the state capitals?
Governors of respective states hoist the national flag on the occasion of Republic Day celebrations in state capitals.
Two national flag ceremonies are held in India.
One on Republic Day and the other on Independence Day.
On the occasion of Independence Day celebrations, the Prime Minister hoists the national flag in the national capital and the Chief Minister in the state capitals.
Who takes the salute at the Republic Day parade in New Delhi?
The President of India takes the salute of the grand parade performed by soldiers on the Republic Day parade.
He is also the Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Armed Forces.
In this parade, the Indian Army displays its new tanks, missiles, radars, etc.
Where is the ceremony called'Beating Retreat'held?
The Beating Retreat is held on the Raisina Hills in front of the Rashtrapati Bhavan, with the President as the chief guest.
The Beating the Retreat ceremony is called the closing ceremony of Republic Day.
The Beating Retreat is held on the evening of 29 January, the third day of the Republic Day celebrations.
In the Beating Retreat, bands from the Army, Air Force, and Navy march, playing traditional tunes.
Who designed the Indian National Flag?
The Indian national flag was designed by Pingali Venkayya.
When Pingali initially designed the flag, it was only two colours, red and green.
He was the flag bearer of the Indian National Congress party.

Under this notification, it was announced to change the last date for linking Aadhaar card with PAN card or Form 60.
Under this amendment, the last date for linking Aadhaar card with bank accounts has now been extended to 31 March 2018.

d_en: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer in women in India.
According to the National Health Portal, India reports 1,22844 new cases of cervical cancer every year, of which 67,477 women die prematurely.
Compared to other countries of the world, India is far behind in terms of preventing this cancer.
According to the World Health Organization, one woman dies from the disease every eight minutes in India.
What is cancer and who can get it?
Periodic vaccination against the HPV virus can prevent the disease in up to 70% of cases.
The lowest, longest equal part of the uterus is the cervix.
It is also called the mouth of the uterus.
The cancer that occurs in this area is called cervical cancer.
Women who are sexually active, usually between the ages of 20 and 50, may be susceptible to the disease.
Poor social and economic conditions, early marriage, frequent pregnancy, malnutrition, lack of hygiene of private parts, etc. increase the chances of transmission of the disease manifold.
In addition, smoking, having sex with more than one person, condoms, and lack of other preventive contraceptive measures increase the risk of the disease.
Human papillomavirus (HPV) virus has been found to be the cause of transmission of this cancer in up to 70% of women.
The virus is transmitted through sexual contact.
Once infected, the virus causes changes in cell structure (DNA) that cause cells to grow uncontrollably and become cancerous.
What are the symptoms of the disease?
The young woman from Surat, who is fighting for her life against cancer, does not understand the symptoms of this disease soon and comes to understand after the infection has progressed a lot.
Often, the initial symptoms are similar to those of other common illnesses and cannot be identified immediately.
Thus, many lives are lost due to the delay in the detection of the disease.
Its symptoms are mostly white discharge, frequent urinary tract infection (disease), persistent abdominal pain, etc.
These symptoms are often persistent, sometimes appearing from time to time.
Similarly, symptoms such as bleeding or pain after sexual intercourse, irregular menstrual periods, etc. are also seen.
So don't ignore these common symptoms.

d_en: Shimla: The construction of the Atal Tunnel at an altitude of 10,000 feet in the Pir Panjal range of Himachal Pradesh has been completed.
This tunnel will be the longest road tunnel in the world which has taken 10 years to build.
It is likely to be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi next month.
It was built because the Manali-Sarchu-Leh route is closed for six months a year due to the Rohtang Pass completely frozen between November and May.

The tunnel will connect Manali to the Lahaul Valley throughout the year and reduce the length of the Manali-Rohtang Pass-Sarchu-Leh road by 46 km. Apart from connecting the people of Lahaul-Spiti with the rest of India, the tunnel will help provide a major strategic advantage to the security forces for further connectivity.
BROATAL TUNNEL The crucial phase of construction of the world's longest road tunnel Atal Tunnel has been completed.
Works related to electro-mechanic fittings including street lighting, ventilation and intelligent traffic control system are also almost complete.
BROATAL TUNNEL The world's longest road tunnel A steel superstructure bridge of 100 meters length is also being prepared across the Chandra River at the northern portal of the tunnel.
But due to the outbreak of the COVID 19 pandemic, the tunnel and other works were stopped for 10 days.

BROATAL TUNNEL The construction of the world's longest road tunnel tunnel is at an important stage so proactive measures have been taken, in which Lieutenant General Harpal Singh, DG Border Roads took up the matter with the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh and proactively recommended to the state government for labour.

d_en: Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to arrive in the national capital on Monday for the 21st India-Russia annual summit.
This will be the first face-to-face meeting between Putin and Prime Minister Narendra Modi since the BRICS summit in November 2019.

A number of agreements are expected to be signed between the two countries to strengthen cooperation in key areas of defence, space technology, trade and investment, arms production sector, energy and technology.
Putin will arrive in Delhi on Monday afternoon while Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu are arriving on Sunday night.

The meeting between PM Modi and Putin will take place at Hyderabad House in Delhi According to the information, Russian President Vladimir Putin will arrive in Delhi on Monday (December 6, 2021) afternoon and will be in India for just 6 to 7 hours.
However, there will be an intensive round of talks between India and Russia at various levels during this period.
The meeting between Russian President Putin and Prime Minister Narendra Modi will take place at around 5.30 pm on Monday at Hyderabad House.
There will also be a session of direct and informal talks between the two leaders.
The number of officials in this interaction between the two countries has also been kept very limited in view of the concerns raised by the Omicron variant of Corona and the COVID protocol.
Putin will also leave on Monday night at around 1: 30 pm.

d_en: The government has introduced 3 bills in Parliament to reform the agricultural sector.
The government has already implemented the rule through ordinance, but since Parliament is now in session, it is also necessary to pass it from Parliament.
There have been protests in many places in Haryana and Punjab over the bill, with Punjab MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal even resigning from the Modi cabinet in protest.
The first bill is about reforming the Essential Commodities Act 2010.
The aim is to transform the agricultural sector through reforms and increase farmers'income.
Farmers have been given the right to stock or sell their crops.
Under the existing Essential Commodities Act, no person can stock essential commodities beyond the prescribed limit.
But the new bill will provide relief to farmers and the bill is said to increase private sector and FDI investment in the agriculture sector.
The bill states that whenever farmers produce more of an essential crop, the price of that crop in the market falls and farmers suffer.
The bill provides for adequate processing arrangements for the farmers'crop to prevent spoilage of the produce.

d_en: New Delhi: A large number of cases of online fraud have started coming to light.
Fraudsters are committing cybercrimes in a number of online ways to target people who are not technology friendly.
Online banking fraud is also one of them.
As digital banking and online transactions are on the rise, the incidence of banking-related cybercrimes is also on the rise.
The government and banks are alerting people to cybercrime at their own level.
However, cybercriminals keep coming up with new ways to cheat people, so very often people fall prey to their tricks.
Such cybercriminals are constantly active.
The Home Ministry of the central government asked people to be careful in this regard and informed about the new method being used by cybercriminals.
People are being texted by thugs to add the nominee to your bank account and say that money can be transferred from your account to the nominee's account after a few minutes.
The message also says at the end, "If you haven't added a nominee, follow the instructions by clicking on the link."
In fact, it is not a link to a bank but a way to gather information necessary for fraud.
The information was shared by the Ministry of Home Affairs on Twitter by Cyber Dost.
Cyber Dost has tweeted to show the format of the message to be sent for cheating and has been told to avoid such messages.
"Such messages can be a trick on the part of cybercriminals to scam you," said the cyber buddy.
Always verify with your bank and avoid clicking on such links.
"If you fall victim to such messages, thugs can also steal money from your account.

d_en: New Delhi: If you travel by booking a ticket on the Indian Railways, then this news is for you.
In fact, the Indian Railways has changed the rules related to train ticket reservation.
This change in train ticket reservation rules is very important for you to know.
But, before we get into your new rule, let's get to know the old rule.
Read - New special trains will run on different routes of the country from Delhi, here is the full information Indian Railways has changed the rule related to the chart made from ticket reservation.
Until now, according to Indian Railways rules, a chart of reserved tickets was created four hours before the train left the station.
But, that will not happen now.
Indian Railways has changed this rule related to train ticket reservation.
Keeping in mind the convenience of the passengers, the Indian Railways has changed the rule of ticket reservation.
As per the new rules, now the second chart of train ticket reservation in the train will be released half an hour i.e. 30 minutes before the train leaves the station.
This will be the final chart of ticket reservation in the train.
This change in the rules made by the Indian Railways has come into effect from 10th October i.e. today.
Now the final chart of ticket reservation in trains has started to be released just 30 minutes before the train leaves the station.
The name on this chart will be confirmed.
This means that the seat in the train will be considered confirmed based on this chart.
This rule will give waiting tickets about three and a half hours more to be confirmed.

The purpose of issuing the second ticket reservation chart half an hour before the train leaves the station is to close online or window ticket bookings on seats left vacant after the first reservation chart.
This will benefit those who have already booked tickets in waiting.

The WHO is already tracking two sub-variants of Omicron, BA.1 and BA.2, which are currently the two most dominant variants in the world.
The WHO says it is important to keep an eye on the two new sub-variants of the corona, as they had additional mutations.
In such a situation, more studies need to be done to know their ability to evade immunity.
Experts believe that both these new sub-variants are likely to be less deadly, but people must follow Covid protocols to prevent them.
Experts also say that it is too early to say how the mutations of these two new sub-variants will affect the corona epidemic.

d_en: Mumbai: There is good news for bank customers.
From April 1, old cheque books, passbooks and Indian Financial Code (IFSC) of a total of 8 banks will be deactivated.
That is, no transaction of any kind can be made from the old cheque book.
Because recently these 8 banks have been merged with other banks.
Significantly, the banking sector will stop old cheques from 1 April due to changes in account numbers, IFSC code, MICR code of account holders due to the merger of banks.
So, customers of such banks should go to the nearest branch and apply for a new passbook and cheque book.
The central government decided to merge the banks due to rising NPAs.
The list of banks includes Dena Bank, Vijaya Bank, Oriental Bank of Commerce, United Bank of India, Syndicate Bank, Andhra Bank, Corporation Bank and Allahabad Bank.
However, only two of these banks, Syndicate Bank and Canara Bank, have seen relief for their customers.
The cheque books of these banks will be valid till 30 June 2021.

d_en: Ahmedabad: Due to the impact of the Western Disturbance, most of the places in Gujarat (Gujarat Weather Update) had a monsoon-like situation for two consecutive days.
Over 100 taluks in the state were inundated and five of them received more than 1 inch of rainfall.
According to the forecast of the Meteorological Department, the weather will still be monsoonal (Gujarat unseasonal rain in winter) today in many places of the state.
Heavy rainfall is forecast for Panchmahal, Dahod, Chhota Udepur, Narmada today.
With this, it is predicted that the cold will increase from today (Gujarat winter).
People shivered in the scorching cold as the day temperature dipped below 20 degrees at most places in the state on Thursday.
According to the forecast of the Meteorological Department, the temperature in Gujarat is expected to increase by 4 degrees from today.

Dabhoi in Vadodara district received the highest rainfall of 2 inches, followed by Dabhoi in Chhota Udepur with 1.5 inches, Tilakwad in Narmada with 1.25 inches and Mangrol in Surat, Garudeshwar in Narmada with more than 1 inch during the day on Thursday.
Chhota Udepur, Sankheda, Jambughoda, Hansot, Ankleshwar, Palsana, Jalod received more than half an inch of rain.

Under the influence of the cold winds, the maximum temperature of Ahmedabad was recorded at 19.3 ° C, 11 ° C below normal, and the minimum temperature was recorded at 16.9 ° C, 3 ° C below normal, in two days.
The city recorded its lowest minimum temperature of 14.3 ° C on 25 November.
Thursday's temperature was recorded below 20 degrees in most places in the state.
Naliya, Vallabh Vidyanagar recorded the lowest minimum temperature at 15.2 degrees.
Elsewhere, Vadodara recorded 15.8 degrees Celsius, Bhavnagar 17.4 degrees Celsius, Bhuj 17.8 degrees Celsius, Rajkot 18.7 degrees Celsius and Surat 16.6 degrees Celsius.

On 24th August, Meet & Kris at\ 1: 00 PM on Ektiva.

d_en: Ahmedabad: The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) has geared up for a possible third wave of coronavirus.
Whether it is hospitals or funeral houses, advance preparations are already underway.
In order to meet the potential third wave, works have been sanctioned to increase beds in SVP Hospital and CNG smash house maintenance.
In this regard, AMC Road and Building Committee Chairman Mahadevbhai Desai said that it has been decided to set up 350 more oxygenated beds in the corporation-run SVP Hospital in Ahmedabad city.
A meeting of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation Road and Building Committee was held.
In which works worth crores of rupees have been approved to increase the oxygen beds (350 new oxygen beds in SVP) in SVP Hospital for the possible third wave of corona in Ahmedabad city.
SVP Hospital was declared a full-fledged Covid hospital in the first and second waves of Corona.
Once again, preparations have been started to set up the system at the SVP Hospital.

AMC is learning a lot from the first and second waves.
Under this, the ASM has now started preparations for a possible third wave from now on.
On the other hand, a meeting of the water committee of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation was held.
Jatinbhai Patel, chairman of the AMC water committee, said that an important decision has been taken regarding the frequent breaking of drainage lids in the city.
